sentences.text: The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/S.166 of M.V. Act against the respondents claiming compensation amount of Rs.3,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petition are as under:
On 20.9.2017 at about 3.20 p.m. the petitioner was pushing his cart on MEI Factory road carefully and cautiously, when he reached near RMC Yard, 6th Gate Junction, at that time a car bearing No.KA-04-3369 being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life and safety of others and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to the impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was shifted to K.C.General Hospital,
Malleshwaram, Bengaluru wherein he took the treatment as an inpatient.

3. Further the contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy,
aged about 47 years, doing a coolie and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.
The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-04-MN-3369.
Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Contending the above facts, he prays to grant for compensation with interest and cost.
4. In response to the petition notice, the respondents have appeared before the court and inspite of sufficient opportunities given to the respondent No.2 has not filed his written statement.
So, the written statement of the respondent No.2 is taken as not filed.
The respondent No.1 has appeared before the court and filed its written statement.
5. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.1 are as under:
The respondent No.1 has contended in its written statement that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further this respondent has denied about the issuance of the policy in respect of vehicle bearing No.KA-03-MN- 3369 and its validity.

Further contended that neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied the mandatory provisions of S.
134 and S. 158(6) of the M.V. Act in furnishing the better particulars.
Further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the same.
Further contended that the accident occurred due to the carelessness on the part of the petitioner himself.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in the claim petition.
Contending the above facts, he prays to dismiss the claim petition as against this respondent with cost.
6. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed:

1 . Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-04-MN-3369 on 20.9.2017 at about 3.20 p.m. near RMC Shri Velu vs Tata Aig General Insurance Co. Ltd on 20 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188464643/
2 Yard, 6th Gate Junction, MEI Factory Road, Bengaluru?

From whom?
3.

7. In order to prove the case, the petitioner himself has examined as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P9.
8.
To disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove the defence, the respondent No.1 has not led any evidence on its behalf.
9. Heard the arguments.

10. My findings to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: In the Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per final order for the following:
R E A S O N S 11. ISSUE NO.1:-
During the course of arguments, the learned counsel for the petitioner argued by reiterating the contents of petition and also evidence put forth by PW1.
Further he argued that the petitioner has proved his case as contended in the petition by producing oral and documentary evidence.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.

12. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has denied the accident in toto, hence,
prays to dismiss the petition as against the respondent No.1.
13. On rival contention urged by both the counsel, I, intend to discuss the merits of the case.
14. In order to prove the case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 and he has stated in his evidence by reiterating the contents of petition.

Further in support of his evidence, he has produced the prosecution papers and the same are marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P6 such as FIR with complaint,
Spot mahazar, rough sketch, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet.
15. On perusal of Ex.P1 complaint reveals that complaint has been lodged by the petitioner on 21.09.2017.

So, based on the complaint, FIR came to be registered by Yeshwanthapura Traffic Police in Cr. No.397/2017 against the driver of the car bearing No.KA04-MN-3369 for the offences punishable u/s 279 and 338 of IPC and S.134 (A & B) R/w S. 187 of IMV Act.
On perusal of Ex.P2 and Ex.P3 are the spot mahazar and sketch also reveals the scene of occurrence and it corroborate the evidence of PW1

. Ex.P4 is the IMV report reveals that no damages found on the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-04-MN-3369 and IMV inspector has opined that the accident was not due to Shri Velu vs Tata Aig General Insurance Co. Ltd on 20 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188464643/
3 mechanical defect of the vehicle.

sentences.text: Ex.P5 is the wound certificate reveals that the petitioner has sustained grievous as well as simple injuries.

Ex.P6 is the charge sheet reveals that after investigation I.O. has filed charge sheet against the driver of the three wheeler goods van for the offences punishable u/s 279 and 338 of IPC and S.134(A & B), R/w S.187 of IMV Act.
16.
The respondent No.1 has contended that the accident occurred due to the carelessness of the petitioner.
To substantiate the said fact, the respondent No.1 has not examined any witness on its behalf.
Moreover he has not challenged the charge sheet filed against the driver of the car.
On the other hand, petitioner has proved his case through oral and documentary evidence.

17. In addenda of this, in a claim for compensation U/S.166 of MV Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others).

sentences.text: 18. Looking to the oral evidence of PW1 and the documents placed before the court, it is clear that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car.
Hence, I answer this issue in the affirmative.
19. ISSUE NO.2:-
The case of the petitioner is that he met with an accident on 20.9.2017 at about 3.20 p.m. and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was shifted to K.C.General Hospital,
wherein he took the treatment as inpatient.

To substantiate the said fact, petitioner has produced wound certificate at Ex.P5, which discloses the following injuries;
1.Swelling, tenderness and deformity over great toe of right foot 2.Abrasion over right elbow measuring 4 cms X 2mc 3.Abrasion over front of left knee measuring 2 cms X 2 cms 4.Abrasion over front middle third of right leg measuring 4 cms x 2 cms 20.
The doctor is of the opinion that the injury No.1 is grievous in nature and rest of the injuries are simple in nature.

The petitioner has produced copy of the discharge summary marked at Ex.P7,
which discloses that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took the treatment as inpatient from 20.9.2017 and discharged on 28.9.2017 and treated conservatively.

21. Considering the oral evidence of PW1 and the documents placed before the court, I am of the opinion that the petitioner might have sustained pain and agony, for which, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.25,000/- under the head of pain and sufferings.
22. The case of the petitioner is that, he was hale and healthy at the time of accident, aged about 47 years, coolie and getting an income of Rs.15,000/- per month.
But he has not produced any documents pertains to his avocation and income.

In the absence of the documents pertains to his Shri Velu vs Tata Aig General Insurance Co. Ltd on 20 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188464643/
4 avocation and income, it is very difficult to assess the income of the petitioner as alleged in the claim petition.

sentences.text: So, considering the present life condition and the age of the petitioner and the year of accident, if notional income of Rs.7,500/- per month is considered, it will meet the ends of justice.
The petitioner has produced discharge summary marked at Ex.P7, which shows that he was admitted from 20.9.2017 and discharged on 28.9.2017.
The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries, he might have taken rest and treatment at least for one month.
Therefore, one month income comes to Rs.7,500/- is granted to the petitioner under the head of loss of income during laid up period and rest period.
23. The contention of the petitioner is that, he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses.
On record he has produced the medical bills marked at Ex.P8 to the extent of Rs.13,105/-.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.13,105/- towards medical expenses.
24. Further contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 47 years, coolie and getting an income of Rs.15,000/- per month.
Due to the accident he is unable to walk for long distance, cannot bear weight on his right leg, cannot climb stairs and often gets pain in his right leg.
The petitioner has not examined the doctor to speak about the grievousness of the injuries or to assess the disability.
The petitioner has produced x-ray at Ex.P9.
Therefore, no amount is granted under this head.
25. Further contention of the petitioner is that the petitioner has sustained fractures.
So his happiness and pleasure will be restricted to some extent.
Further PW1 has stated in his evidence that due to the accident he took the treatment as inpatient.
To substantiate the said fact, the petitioner has produced discharge summary marked at Ex.P7, which shows that he was admitted from 20.9.2017 and discharged on 28.9.2017.
So, one must attend him during the above said period.

Considering the above facts and looking to the period of hospitalization, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.15,000/- under the head of amenities attendant,
conveyance, food and nourishment etc.
26.

Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reason, I am of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads:

Medical expenses Rs.13,105-00 4. Loss of future income Nil 5. Amenities, Attendant, Rs.15,000-00 Nourishment and conveyance charges Total Rs.60,605-00 27.
LIABILITY:

On perusal of the contents of petition and contents of written statement, it reveals that, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the car bearing Shri Velu vs Tata Aig General Insurance Co. Ltd on 20 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188464643/

sentences.text: The respondent No.1 has denied about the issuance of the policy in respect of car bearing No.KA-04-MN-3369 and its validity.
But on perusal of the cause title of the claim petition the period of policy was from 12.9.2017 to 11.9.2018.
The accident occurred on 20.9.2017.
The same has not been challenged by the respondent No.1.
So, one thing is clear that as on the date of accident the policy was in existence.
Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 8% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 in partly affirmative.
29. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of above discussion on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of MV act is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.60,605/- with interest @ 8% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 8% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of compensation amount together with interest, entire amount shall be released to the petitioner through account payee cheque on proper identification without any further proceedings.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer online, corrected by me and then pronounced in open court on this the 20th day of April 2019).
(MAHANTESH S.DARGAD) III ADDL.SMALL CAUSES JUDGE & XXIX ACMM, BANGALORE.
